title: Selling a Rental in November? Your 1031 Clock Shrinks

scenes.vo: Sell a rental this month? Your 1031 clock could lose a month.

captions.text: Your 1031 clock could lose a month.

scenes.vo: A 1031 exchange defers tax on a rental's gain when you reinvest in real estate.

captions.text: A 1031 exchange defers tax on a rental's gain
when you reinvest in real estate.

scenes.vo: Name the replacement in 45 days. Close within 180, or by your tax deadline, if sooner.

captions.text: or by your tax deadline, if sooner.

scenes.vo: Sell November seventeenth: day 180 is May sixteenth. Returns are due April fifteenth.
That's 31 days gone. Selling late? Ask your tax pro about an extension.

captions.text: Selling late? Ask your tax pro about an extension.

scope.value: Real property held for business or investment (since 2018)
scope.source: IRS, 2026 Instructions for Form 8824, published 2026-11-09, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8824.pdf

identifyDays.unit: days after transfer of relinquished property to identify replacement

receiveDays.unit: days after transfer, or the tax return due date incl. extensions, whichever is earlier

returnDueDate.unit: due date of 2026 calendar-year individual returns for most people (extension to 2027-10-15 via Form 4868)

exampleDay45.unit: sale date + 45 days, computed in scenes/math.ts

exampleDay180.unit: sale date + 180 days, computed in scenes/math.ts

exampleDueDay.unit: days from sale to Apr 15, 2027, computed in scenes/math.ts

daysLost.unit: days between Apr 15 and May 16, 2027 (lost without an extension), computed in scenes/math.ts

cutoffSale.unit: a sale on this date has day 180 = Apr 15, 2027; later sales are cut short (calendar-year individual, Apr 15 due date)

notes: Educational only, not tax advice. Assumes a calendar-year individual with an April 15, 2027 due date (from the IRS DRAFT 2026 Form 4868); disaster postponements could change it.
Does not cover qualified intermediaries, boot or related-party rules, and does not claim weekends/holidays extend 1031 deadlines.
VO text keeps '1031'; read aloud as 'ten thirty-one'.
